name: Miriam Katz

five_sec.what_is_it: An app that decides what's for dinner for you.
five_sec.who_for: Families who want someone else to pick dinner.
five_sec.trust_why: 90,000 families is a real number. 'Letter from the CEO' as the main button tells me nothing.
five_sec.next_step: Find the diet options. If kosher isn't there, I'm done.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It's an app screen with a menu on it, not a box.

full_page.what_stopped_me: The word kosher does not appear. 'Ollie uses AI... to write a recipe just for you.' An AI writing recipes for a kosher kitchen is how you end up with chicken in cream sauce.
full_page.whats_missing: Kosher. Meat versus dairy. Household size. A straight price on this page; the meals page says 'prices when you download the app' and another page says $25 a month.

OL.quote: An AI that writes my recipes and never once says kosher. No.

five_sec.what_is_it: A recipe organizer with a planning calendar and grocery list.
five_sec.who_for: People who cook from their own recipes.
five_sec.trust_why: Real ratings on both app stores, no card for the trial, and it looks like it's been around.
five_sec.next_step: See if it can import from the kosher sites I already use.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Recipes and lists. The picture is someone writing in a notebook.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Nothing serious. It doesn't know kosher either, but it doesn't have to: I clip my own recipes, so nothing mixes meat and dairy unless I put it there. Price is fine.
full_page.whats_missing: Suggestions. I'd still do the deciding. A way to tag nights as meat or dairy would be nice; I assume I can use notes on the calendar.

PTE.quote: Recipe clipper, calendar, shared with the household, no card. It doesn't understand kosher, but it doesn't pretend to. I can work with that.

five_sec.what_is_it: Texts the family dinner ideas, they vote, and it builds the grocery list for Instacart.
five_sec.who_for: Families with kids who'd answer a text. My teens would.
five_sec.trust_why: 'No card needed' and 'We don't deliver food' are direct. I like direct. I don't know the company.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: 'We don't deliver food. We plan your week and send your grocery list.' Bold, right there.

full_page.what_stopped_me: No kosher. The diet talk is 'dietary needs,' and the footer has gluten-free, diabetic, Mediterranean, but nothing about meat and dairy. The sample week has taco night and meatballs; in most houses taco night means beef and cheese together. I can't tell.
full_page.whats_missing: Kosher as a real setting, meat or dairy marked on each dinner, and whether it plans for seven. The sample is a family of four.

DD.quote: Clear page, I'll say that. But 'dietary needs' isn't kosher. Will it put cheese on the taco night with ground beef? Nobody says.

five_sec.next_step: Go straight to the list of plans.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: A phone surrounded by food drawings.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Fifteen plans, no kosher. The home page shows Pork Chops, Shrimp Po' Boys and Cheesy Bacon-Wrapped Chicken. Three treif dinners in one scroll.
full_page.whats_missing: Kosher. A price on the home page.

EM.quote: Shrimp po' boys and bacon-wrapped chicken on the front page. That answers my question.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal kit boxes, with a pop-up game.
five_sec.who_for: People who want food shipped to them.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Open A Box To Reveal Your Offer.' I'm not playing a game to find a price.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: HelloFresh boxes and plates of food.

full_page.what_stopped_me: The meat isn't kosher and the menu is pork sausage, bacon, steak with garlic herb butter. For seven people it would cost a fortune anyway.
full_page.whats_missing: Anything kosher. A price before my zip code.

HF.quote: Steak with herb butter, bacon soup, a mystery box. Not for a kosher house of seven.

dd_offer.why: No card, back to the free plan, email three days before. Very plain.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: The texting and family features stop and I'm on the free version. Nothing charged because they never had my card.

head_to_head.reason: It's my own kosher recipes, so it can't suggest something I'd never serve.

OL.reason: DinnerDrop is clearer and cheaper, and Ollie's AI is even less likely to get meat and dairy right.

PTE.reason: Plan to Eat lets me control every recipe; DinnerDrop picks for me without knowing kosher.

EM.reason: eMeals shows treif on the front page; DinnerDrop at least doesn't.

HF.reason: HelloFresh ships non-kosher meat; DinnerDrop lets me buy meat at the kosher store.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Pricing page (/start) diet FAQ and the sample week on the home page: if DinnerDrop can do it, name kosher as a setting, label each dinner meat, dairy or pareve, and say it plans for 7+. Without the word kosher I leave at the diet list.
